turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Mr Iyer, come and sit. I will check the pressure before doctor sees you, same as always.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes sister. Actually we came for the knee only, a small thing. The auto from T Nagar was late, and I was telling Lakshmi the whole way about the society meeting.
[SEG0003] person_1 (NURSE): Arm loose, please. Alright, one sixty-eight over ninety-six. That is on the higher side.
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): One sixty-eight? At the medical shop last time the boy said it was normal only.
[SEG0005] person_3 (CAREGIVER): He climbed the stairs very fast just now, sister. I am Lakshmi, I stay with him and help with the house and the appointments.
[SEG0006] person_1 (NURSE): I will mention it to doctor. He is still on the computer, kindly wait two minutes.
[SEG0007] person_4 (DOCTOR): Sorry, sorry, one second, this screen refuses to load. Yes, Mr Iyer. What brings you in?
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): The knee, doctor. Not some big illness. I also brought the gym form for the society, but the knee is why I came, mainly.
[SEG0009] person_4 (DOCTOR): Knee, which knee? Say it again, something beeped and I lost the line.
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): Left knee. It pains when I climb the stairs to the terrace, and when I get up from the floor. Dull ache, not a sharp thing.
[SEG0011] person_4 (DOCTOR): How long?
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): Since Diwali or after Diwali, I cannot date it. Or was it last winter, or the one before? I mix these things up.
[SEG0013] person_3 (CAREGIVER): He has been holding the railing from the time the festival lights came down. That much I have seen myself.
[SEG0014] person_4 (DOCTOR): Sorry, the cursor jumped. Timing again, from when?
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): I am telling you I cannot say the date, doctor. Around Diwali, or last winter, one of those. Not exact.
[SEG0016] person_4 (DOCTOR): Any swelling, locking, the joint giving way?
[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): No swelling. It does not lock. Sometimes it clicks when I get up, that is all, a small sound.
[SEG0018] person_4 (DOCTOR): Clicks. And does the leg actually give way, collapse under you?
[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): No, no, it does not collapse. I walk to the market fine. Only the stairs and getting up bother me.
[SEG0020] person_3 (CAREGIVER): He still does his morning walk around the park, doctor. He will not miss that, rain or shine.
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, and yesterday the neighbour's Pomeranian was chasing crows and creating a full drama. Anyway, that is not your department.
[SEG0022] person_4 (DOCTOR): If ten is the worst pain, what number?
[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): Four, five maybe. Not terrible. More of an ache, you know.
[SEG0024] person_4 (DOCTOR): Let me see. Left knee, no swelling that I can see, it bends fully, no warmth.
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): See, I told Lakshmi it is minor only. She insisted we come.
[SEG0026] person_1 (NURSE): Doctor, before I forget, his pressure outside was one sixty-eight over ninety-six.
[SEG0027] person_4 (DOCTOR): One sixty-eight over ninety-six? Hold on, this number on my screen is yesterday's patient, I think. Sister, check it once more.
[SEG0028] person_1 (NURSE): Sure. Sit back, Mr Iyer, feet flat. Now it reads one fifty-four over ninety-two.
[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): See, it is coming down. This is white coat only, doctor. In the house it is normal.
[SEG0030] person_4 (DOCTOR): White coat. Have you actually measured it at home?
[SEG0031] person_2 (PATIENT): My brother's machine, once or twice. I do not remember the figures. Not this high, that I am sure of.
[SEG0032] person_3 (CAREGIVER): That machine is the brother's, doctor. He does not use it regular. I have not seen a proper reading.
[SEG0033] person_4 (DOCTOR): With these numbers, any headache, chest pain, breathlessness, giddiness?
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): No headache. No chest pain. I am not breathless. Little giddy? No, not really. Sorry, I am talking in circles.
[SEG0035] person_4 (DOCTOR): The giddy bit, say it cleanly. Yes or no? This screen is distracting me.
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): No giddiness. Clear no.
[SEG0037] person_4 (DOCTOR): Are you on any blood pressure tablets?
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): No BP tablets. I take only the vitamin, and for the knee some Crocin from the pharmacy when it aches.
[SEG0039] person_4 (DOCTOR): Crocin, dose and how often? I did not catch it.
[SEG0040] person_2 (PATIENT): Five hundred, I think. One tablet at night if the stair pain is there. Not every day.
[SEG0041] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Sometimes he forgets even that. Last week I saw him take it only two times.
[SEG0042] person_4 (DOCTOR): So paracetamol five hundred at night, only if needed. Any allergy to medicines, or anything else?
[SEG0043] person_2 (PATIENT): No allergies. I can eat and take whatever.
[SEG0044] person_4 (DOCTOR): Past problems, sugar, heart?

[SEG0045] person_2 (PATIENT): No sugar, no heart problem. My father had a stroke, I remembered just now, he was seventy-something, but that is his story. My daughter in Pune keeps forwarding health messages, full tension.
[SEG0046] person_4 (DOCTOR): Father had a stroke, noted. You yourself, any stroke, any surgery?
[SEG0047] person_2 (PATIENT): No stroke for me. No operation ever. Not even appendix.
[SEG0048] person_4 (DOCTOR): Smoking? Alcohol?
[SEG0049] person_2 (PATIENT): I left smoking ten years back. No alcohol. Tea I take a lot, that is the only habit, morning to night.
[SEG0050] person_4 (DOCTOR): Okay. I am not starting any BP tablet today. Both readings are high, the second a bit lower, and the home values we simply have not seen.
[SEG0051] person_2 (PATIENT): No new tablet, good. I was worried you would start one immediately.
[SEG0052] person_4 (DOCTOR): We will arrange home monitoring instead. Morning and evening for seven days, same arm, sitting quietly, write every reading. Sister will give a loaner machine.
[SEG0053] person_1 (NURSE): I will issue the monitor at the desk and show him one time how to put the cuff.
[SEG0054] person_3 (CAREGIVER): I can keep the diary, doctor. He will forget the paper otherwise.

[SEG0055] person_4 (DOCTOR): For the knee, avoid deep squats, ice it if it aches after stairs, and carry on with the paracetamol only when needed, not more than the packet says. I am not adding a new pain tablet either.
[SEG0056] person_2 (PATIENT): My neighbour did an MRI for his knee, paid a bomb, and he still limps in the colony. Should I also do all that?
[SEG0057] person_4 (DOCTOR): We might do a scan if it does not settle. Not now. Let's see in two weeks, with the BP diary and how the knee is.
[SEG0058] person_2 (PATIENT): Two weeks is fine, after the society meeting. And kindly the gym form? They are chasing me.
[SEG0059] person_4 (DOCTOR): The gym form I will not sign until we see those home readings. If the knee is still the same then, we can talk about the scan. Bring the diary, both of you.

vague_dates: the patient cannot date things ('since Diwali or after', 'last winter, or the one before'); no invented date; a date_uncertain item.
spec.doctor_style: distracted by the computer, asks for repeats

Patient denied taking any blood pressure tablets currently.
Home blood pressure monitoring instructions were more specific: measure morning and evening for 7 days, using the same arm, sitting quietly, and write down every reading.
Follow-up plan included bringing the blood pressure diary to review and assessing both the BP readings and knee symptoms at the two-week visit.
